questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
Stop only to let other traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely. Let all traffic and pedestrians pass. Then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell drivers about dangers ahead. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopping at an intersection to:

options.text: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
Look for dark clouds that mean bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if drivers behind you see you stopping.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors to see vehicles coming from behind. Make sure drivers notice you and your actions. This keeps you safe at intersections.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, you should:

options.text: Focus only on your riding, not your surroundings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright or reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you easier to see. This reduces crash risk. Always watch other drivers and be ready for what they do.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield to you.
Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a position where other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, change your lane position to be more visible. This helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: Keeping space between you and other vehicles helps because:

options.text: You can ride behind other vehicles more easily.
You have more time to react to what other drivers do.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what other drivers do.
questions.explanation: Space around your motorcycle is important. If danger appears, you have time to react and room to move safely.

questions.question: To be seen better by other road users, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear brightly-colored clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors like orange, red, yellow, or green. Reflective materials also help make you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: Your chance of surviving a crash improves if you wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: A DOT-compliant helmet.
questions.explanation: A helmet that meets DOT and state standards gives the best head and neck protection. A good-quality helmet that fits properly is the single best way to survive a crash.

questions.question: When the lights on this sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for the train to pass.
questions.explanation: When lights flash at a railroad crossing, stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to beat a train.

questions.question: When riding, you should wear:
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors even during the day to help other drivers see you. Reflective clothing also helps improve visibility.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of head or neck injury?
questions.correctAnswerText: By wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: Head and neck injuries are always possible when riding a motorcycle, no matter your speed. Wearing a quality helmet that fits properly greatly reduces this risk.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcyclists?
questions.correctAnswerText: Sturdy boots.
questions.explanation: Leather boots protect your feet the most when riding. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle with a passenger, what should you do?

options.text: Ride a little faster than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Merge into smaller gaps of traffic than you normally would.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. This extra weight makes the bike respond more slowly. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. You should reduce speed, start slowing earlier, and look for larger traffic gaps.

questions.question: What is the danger of wind noise when riding?

options.text: It is easy to get used to.
It may cause permanent hearing damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: It may cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise exposure can permanently damage your hearing. Use ear plugs or other hearing protection when riding.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Not make sudden movements, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not make sudden movements, if possible.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, sudden speed or direction changes can cause a skid. Accelerate, shift gears, turn, and brake as smoothly as possible.

questions.question: How can you reduce fatigue on a long trip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Limit your riding per day.
questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks to rest, even if you do not feel tired. Most experienced riders limit riding to six hours per day. Wind, cold, and rain make you tire faster, so dress to protect yourself from the elements.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, what should they do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a quick stop, apply both brakes at the same time. Watch the road ahead to avoid needing sudden stops.

questions.question: As you approach a blind intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Move into the part of the lane that allows other drivers to most easily see you.
Move into the part of the lane closest to the traffic control device.
Move into the outside edge of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the part of the lane that allows other drivers to most easily see you.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane where other drivers can see you as early as possible.

questions.question: How can you get sober after drinking alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: Wait.
questions.explanation: Time is the only way to sober up. Your body must remove the alcohol on its own. Nothing can speed up this process.

questions.question: What should you check before every ride?

options.text: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
Make sure the paint on the bike is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your bike's brake lights work properly.
questions.explanation: Perform safety checks before each ride. Test your brake controls to make sure each one activates the brake lights.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Keep riding. The danger is over.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop and remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object, pull off the road and check your tires and rims for damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the chain or belt before you ride again.

questions.question: What is true about footrests?

options.text: The driver and passenger can share them.
They are required for both the driver and passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are required for both the driver and passenger.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. A motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Firm footing keeps your passenger from falling and pulling you off too.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from your body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time will remove alcohol from your body. There is no way to speed up this process.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?
questions.correctAnswerText: Let them pass you.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.
